newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up, trade buying, early CBOT gains.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up, trade buying, early CBOT gains.

text.p: WCE canola futures settled mostly higher, lifted by moderate commercial buying as well as spillover strength from early gains in CBOT soyoil, floor traders said.
"Commercials were on both sides of the market, but we saw good commercial buying over the day," one floor trader said.
Some producer hedging was noted, which helped to limit gains, floor traders said.
Volume in flaxseed trade was described as heavy. Gains in CBOT wheat spurred some commercial house short covering, but local selling in late trade pushed the market to end mostly lower, traders said.

January canola settled up $2.20 at $411.70. Other contracts were $1.00 lower to $2.50 higher. Feed wheat closed up $0.30 to down $1.20, with December down $0.30 at $176.20. Flaxseed settled steady to down $0.60, with January down $0.10 at $366.90. Western barley closed down $0.30 to $2.00, with February down $0.80 at $145.20.

Commercial short covering in May and July feed peas prompted gains in those contracts, traders said. Volume was very light in December. December settled unchanged at US $201, and May closed up US$2 at $199.
Traders noted a "reversal type day" in western barley. That market opened higher following CBOT wheat, but local and hedge selling late pressured futures at the close, traders said.
Oats did not trade but some commercials sought to arbitrage a higher open in CBOT oat futures, traders said.
(All values in Canadian dollars except peas, oats).
